newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hesse for strict testing of EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hesse for strict testing of EMU criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said on Tuesday the qualification criteria for the planned European economic and monetary union (EMU) should be strictly applied.
Addressing a bank forum on the subject of EMU, Hesse said neither Germany nor France should expect any special treatment when their economic performance came to be tested.
"If Germany fails than Germany should not be accepted," Hesse said.
But Hesse said it would not be good for Europe and economically not opportune if the two countries did not belong to the EMU member states.
Hesse said he personally had not considered the possibility of the failure of the currency union.
The expectation the euro currency would be weaker than the mark was irrational.
Hesse added that the Bundesbank would continue on its course of stability in the run up to the hand over of control to the planned European Central Bank.
